userReference.description: The internal user reference for this depot. Typically a employee or student id of the system

authValues.description: auth values to use for authenticating the user or session. For an issuer service with internal `verifiable_presentation` auth, one value per rule of its `verifiablePresentationAuthRules`, at the rule's `valueIndex`. Each value must have its rule's `valueType`, and its `valueFormat` if the rule has one, and a string must not be blank. Strings are trimmed and lower-cased before they are checked and matched, and numbers and booleans are used as they are. Values of different types never match, so `"12345"` never matches `12345`.

deferredCredentials.description: Whether the depot's credentials may come later. A wallet with nothing to claim then waits until depots/resolve-deferred-credentials is called. Only allowed for issuer service depots, and can't be changed

expectedCredentialTypes.description: The credential types the depot may receive

preauthCodeExpiresIn.description: How long each pre-authorized code of the depot lasts, from the `issue-links/refresh` that makes it: a number of seconds from 1 to 315360000 (10 years), such as `600` for 10 minutes, or `never` for codes that don't expire. Without it, the depot's codes last as long as the Hub's `PREAUTH_CODE_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS` says at each refresh, 259200 (72 hours) by default. A wallet waiting for a depot's deferred credentials authenticates again with the same code when they're ready, so the lifetime must cover the time the issuer takes to add them. Can't be changed

FindDepots.title: Find depots
FindDepots.description: Payload schema for finding depots. The filters combine with AND, and mean what they mean in the depots/get query. authValues requires the serviceId of an internal verifiable_presentation issuer service

authValues.description: Finds the depots whose auth values equal any of these. Each item holds one depot's auth values, as depots/create takes them: one value per auth rule, in valueIndex order. They match as authentication matches them: strings trimmed and lower-cased, numbers and booleans unchanged. Only depots created under the service's current auth rules match

Length of time the disclosure agreement will last.  Duration can be any length of time.

Follows the ISO 8601 standard on durations for time intervals.

Format:

PxYxMxWxD

Where:
x = an integer
Y = Years
M = Months
W = Weeks
D = Days

A valid format requires "P" plus at least one integer and time unit.

Examples: 
P60D = 60 days
P1Y30D = 1 year and 30 days.

presentationDefinition.description: A spec compliant presentation definition. https://identity.foundation/presentation-exchange/#presentation-definition. Not allowed when `authMethods` include `verifiable_presentation`

deactivationDate.description: can be configured to deactivate at a predetermined time or to be deactivated on demand by setting this to now

authMethods.description:
the auth method indicates what authentication method(s) are supported for issuer. To use `preauth` requires the issuer to include a `vendorOriginContext` in the deep link. `verifiable_presentation` requires a `disclosureRequest` and at least one of `verifiablePresentationAuthRules`, and forbids a `presentationDefinition`.
In the future an issuer will be able to use both methods in one disclosure
`authMethods` is required with at least one entry

authMode.description: the auth mode. Currently only `internal` is supported

verifiablePresentationAuthRules.description:
verifiablePresentationAuthRules are the matcher rules that can be used to match an exchange with submitted presentation used for authentication. Required when the authMethods include `verifiable_presentation` and the authMode is `internal`. At most 10 rules.

Each rule reads values of its `valueType` from the presented credentials of its `type`, and ignores values of any other type rather than converting them. Strings are trimmed and lower-cased, and numbers and booleans are used as they are. A depot matches when its `authValues`, normalized the same way, equal the values the rules read, each at its rule's `valueIndex`. Values of different types never match, so `"12345"` never matches `12345`.

path.description: Claims path pointers (OpenID4VP 1.0, section 7), tried in order on each credential of the rule's `type`. The first pointer that selects anything supplies the values. A pointer is an array of segments: a string selects that key of an object, a non-negative integer selects that index of an array, and null selects every element of an array. Only string, number and boolean values are used. For example `[["credentialSubject", "email"], ["credentialSubject", "emails", null]]`

rule.description: how the rule uses the values its path finds. `pick` uses every value found. `equal` uses a value only when exactly one distinct value is found

valueIndex.description: the position of this rule's value in a depot's `authValues`. The rules' value indexes must be exactly 0 to n-1, each used once

type.description: the credential type that the rule reads. It must be one of the `disclosureRequest` types

valueType.description: the JSON type of the rule's values. A depot's auth value at the rule's `valueIndex` must have this type. Values of another type that the rule reads from a credential are ignored, never converted

valueFormat.description: the format of a `string` rule's values, which depots/create checks after trimming the value: `email` is an email address, checked as AJV's `email` format, and `e164` is a phone number in E.164 format, such as `+15556192191`. It doesn't change how values are read or matched. Only allowed when `valueType` is `string`

challengesExpireIn.description: how many seconds before challenges issued by this service expire. Default is 10 minutes

credentialTypesAvailable.description: the types of credentials available from this service
